issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect an instance method named swiftExperienceDescription() on Developer, but the template defines a method named getExperienceDescription(). Additionally, the template's initializer contains a TODO that instructs calling swiftExperienceDescription(). This name/signature mismatch will confuse students about which method to implement and which name to call from the initializer (they may implement swiftExperienceDescription() per the spec while the template leaves an unused getExperienceDescription()).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template's method name match the problem statement and solution. Rename the template extension method getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription(), and ensure the initializer's TODO calls print(self.swiftExperienceDescription()). Alternatively, if getExperienceDescription() was intentional, update the problem statement and solution to use getExperienceDescription() consistently. This keeps method names/signatures consistent across all artifacts and avoids student confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies an instance method named `swiftExperienceDescription()` for the Developer class, and the solution implements that exact method name. The template, however, declares the method as `getExperienceDescription()`. This is a naming mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the developer's Swift experience description) and will confuse students: they may implement or call the wrong method name and tests/client code expecting `swiftExperienceDescription()` will fail or appear missing.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the template method `getExperienceDescription()` to `swiftExperienceDescription()` in template_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift and update any calls (e.g., the initializer print) to use `swiftExperienceDescription()`. This aligns the template with the problem statement and the provided solution, removing the naming mismatch students would otherwise need to resolve.
